title: Rulebook
description: AIP schema for reference skills that are consulted rather than run: conventions, notation, and decision aids that other skills comply with. Rules carry their rationale and, where one exists, the validator that mechanically enforces them - so a rule left to good intentions is visible as one. Lookup tables are referenced as assets, never typed here.

id.description: Short kebab-case identifier, unique within this rulebook, so another skill can cite the rule without quoting it.

rule.description: The rule as an instruction. Imperative, and specific enough to be complied with or not.

rationale.description: Why the rule exists. A rule whose reason is unwritten is one nobody can judge an exception against.

applies_to.description: Optional. What the rule governs, where it is narrower than the rulebook's own scope.

enforced_by.description: Optional. The validator or script that mechanically checks this rule. Its absence is the useful signal: the rule holds only by good intentions, and the corpus can be queried for how many do.

carve_outs.description: Optional. Cases the rule deliberately does not cover, so a reader can tell an exception from an oversight.

purpose.description: What the rulebook encapsulates as a coherent unit of work — the scope it covers and what it adds beyond general agent knowledge. One short paragraph.

trigger_when.description: Conditions under which the agent should consider this skill. Mixed granularity expected — immediate invocation triggers (e.g., 'user asks to add functionality') alongside broader applicability contexts (e.g., 'evaluating technology choices') belong in the same list.

do_not_use_when.description: Optional. Conditions under which the agent should NOT use this skill — explicit non-purposes that pair with trigger_when to sharpen activation. Helps the agent calibrate when adjacent skills or general reasoning would serve better.

applies_to.description: Optional. The artifacts these rules govern - paths, document kinds, or model layers.

complied_with_by.description: Optional. Skills that must comply with this rulebook. A rulebook realizes no process; it is a constraint on the skills that do, and naming them makes that relation queryable rather than implied.

tables.description: Optional. Lookup tables the rules depend on, referenced as assets rather than typed here. A table an agent would read at runtime to pick a value belongs in a file that scripts can read too, so that one fact has one place.

asset.description: Relative path under assets/ to the data file.

consumed_by.description: Optional. Scripts or validators that read the same file, which is the reason it is a file.

references.description: Optional. Supporting documents loaded on demand, so the body stays inside its token budget.

when_to_load.description: The condition under which the agent should read it. A reference with no stated trigger is either never loaded or always loaded, and both defeat the purpose.

scenarios.description: Optional. Worked examples applying the rules to concrete cases. Documentation, not a runtime decision table.

need.description: The situation the rules are applied to.

action.description: Which rule was applied, and how.

anti_patterns.description: Optional. Common mistakes the rulebook steers the agent away from. Concrete corrections to errors the agent would otherwise make.
